traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria and requirements in docs/stories/009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS.story.md are fully implemented and verified. - Core Functionality: detectStaleAnnotations and CLI `detect` identify stale @story references; updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, and CLI `update` update them (individually and in batch). verifyAnnotations and CLI `verify` confirm post-maintenance validity; generateMaintenanceReport and CLI `report` summarize stale references. - Quality Standards: update operations perform narrow, regex-based replacements on @story paths only, write files only when content changes, and do not alter executable code or surrounding formatting. Detection, verification, and reporting are read-only. - Integration: Maintenance tools are exposed as a `maintenance` export from the plugin (src/index.ts) and as the `traceability-maint` CLI via package.json `bin`. Tests exercise both API and CLI in realistic filesystem scenarios. - User Experience: The CLI provides clear commands, help text, success/failure messages, JSON modes for tooling, and distinct exit codes (0/1/2). Messages in tests confirm users see understandable feedback for all commands and error cases. - Error Handling: Code handles non-existent roots, file read failures, permission errors, invalid CLI options (including invalid --format), missing required flags, and unsafe/malicious story paths without crashing, returning appropriate exit codes and diagnostics instead. - Documentation: README and user-docs/api-reference.md both document the maintenance API and CLI, with command descriptions, options, behavior notes, and examples. Combined with the passing, story-tagged tests, this satisfies the story’s Definition of Done for implementation, testing, and documentation.
